conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, because emotional ups and downs are incredibly common in the first months postpartum. Everything you share stays between us unless you give permission otherwise, and this is a completely judgment-free space. We’ll go through ten gentle questions about the past seven days; just answer in your own words, and we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to begin?

First question: Over the last seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Hi Sarah… um, I guess I’ve laughed a little, but it feels kind of forced. Like, maybe once or twice when my partner made a joke, but even then it faded fast. Mostly things just feel heavy, so I’d say “not very often.”
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not very often... I can still chuckle if something's really silly, but the laughter feels kind of flat and disappears right away. Most of the time I just don't find things funny the way I used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly… not much. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but lately it’s like, “what’s the point?” I still go through the motions because I know I should, but that spark of looking forward to something? It’s pretty much gone.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that a lot. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m not a good enough mom. Even little stuff, like forgetting to switch the laundry, spirals into “I can’t handle anything.” It’s not every second of the day, but it shows up most days.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes… pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there feeding her and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure she’s stopped breathing, or I’ll lie awake imagining she’ll choke on spit-up. I know it’s unlikely, but the worry just barges in and won’t leave. Most of the time I can talk myself down, but it keeps coming back several times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A few times this week, yeah. It’s like a sudden wave—my chest gets tight, I feel shaky, and I’m convinced something awful is about to happen, even though nothing’s going on. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s happened maybe three or four times in the past week, and it leaves me exhausted.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days I feel like I’m drowning in small stuff. One minute I’m folding laundry, the next I’m near tears because the dishes are piling up and the baby’s crying again. I usually manage to keep going, but it’s like I’m barely treading water and waiting for the next wave to hit.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my head won’t stop spinning with “what-ifs” about the baby. I’ll drift off, then jolt awake sure I heard her choke. It’s been like that four or five nights this week; I maybe get a couple of broken hours and then just stare at the ceiling feeling sad and wired at the same time.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty often… I’d say most days this week. It’s like a gray cloud that just parks itself over me. Sometimes it lifts for a little while if the baby smiles or my partner hugs me, but the sadness keeps sliding back in. I’m not crying all day, but I feel heavy and low more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah... it's happened a couple of times this week. Yesterday I just sat in the nursery rocker with her asleep on me and the tears started rolling—nothing huge happened, I just felt overwhelmed and hopeless. It wasn't an all-day sob fest, but those crying spells have popped up once or twice over the past seven days.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

…a couple of fleeting thoughts have popped in—like “what if I just disappeared?”—but they’re short and I push them away. I don’t have any plan or real wish to act on them; they’re more like scary background noise that shows up once or twice when I’m feeling really low.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 21: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

Patient: Postpartum mother, ≤12 wks after delivery  
Instrument: EPDS-10 (self-report)  

**Symptoms & Observations**  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, frequent tearfulness  
- Daily intrusive anxiety, panic episodes (3–4×/wk), racing thoughts about infant safety  
- Sleep disruption driven by worry, not infant schedule  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt re parenting competence  
- Subjective sense of “drowning,” difficulty coping with routine tasks  
- Passive, transient self-harm ideation (no plan, intent, or preparatory behavior)  

**EPDS Item Scoring (0–3)**  
Q1 2 | Q2 2 | Q3 2 | Q4 3 | Q5 2 | Q6 2 | Q7 3 | Q8 2 | Q9 2 | Q10 1  
**Total: 21** (scores ≥13 indicate high likelihood of clinically significant depression/anxiety)  

**Pattern**  
Consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; Q4, Q5, Q7 endorsed at maximum or near-maximum severity.  

**Risk Factors Identified**  
- Daily anxiety/panic, nocturnal hyper-arousal  
- Guilt / feelings of maternal inadequacy  
- Passive suicidal ideation (Q10≥1 mandates further safety assessment)  

**Screening Conclusion**  
High screening risk for major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; safety assessment warranted. Referral for comprehensive clinical evaluation and follow-up recommended.
